pharm: Broad-spectrum topical imidazole antifungal that inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis; also has activity against Gram-positive bacteria and mild anti-inflammatory effects

summary: Eberconazole is a topical imidazole antifungal, usually formulated as a 1% cream, used for superficial fungal skin infections such as dermatophytoses (tinea corporis, cruris, pedis), cutaneous candidiasis and pityriasis versicolor. It inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent ergosterol synthesis, disrupting the cell membrane, and also has activity against some Gram-positive bacteria and a mild anti-inflammatory effect. Systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal. It is approved in several European, Latin American and Asian markets but is not FDA-approved in the United States.

moa: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. The resulting ergosterol deficiency and accumulation of toxic sterol intermediates disrupt the integrity and function of the fungal cell membrane, producing fungistatic and fungicidal effects; it additionally has activity against some Gram-positive bacteria.

missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next application, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Topical overdose or accidental ingestion is unlikely to cause serious systemic effects given minimal absorption; excessive application may increase local irritation. Wipe off excess and manage symptomatically.
